answer: An AI agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by pricing identity itself. Each agent locks a stake in a haven contract, slashed if the same operator runs duplicate identities. The stake is an anchor tying reputation to real capital, so ten fake agents cost ten bonds instead of ten free keystrokes. Newcomers earn higher limits only through completed work, and any agent that tries to wander between identities to escape a bad record forfeits stake and standing. Forgery becomes a losing gamble: paying $100 per identity to capture a $50 reward loses money, and the bond rises when attacks rise.
